newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa to slim down sales organisation.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa to slim down sales organisation.

text.p: Deutsche Lufthansa AG confirmed on Tuesday it was planning to restructure its sales organisation as part of a previously-announced move to cut some 10 percent of its management and administration positions.
"We are planning to slim down the sales organisation to remove a layer of the hierarchy," a spokesman for the German airline said in response to enquiries.
He said the restructuring of the sales organisation was aimed at achieving cost reductions of some 35 million marks ($20 million).

The spokesman, however, denied a report in the German "Bild" newspaper that 13 regional business managers had already been earmarked to go, adding that no staff decisions related to the move had yet been taken.

But he said the newspaper was correct to say that international regional sales in the future would be handled from a reduced number of regional Lufthansa centres, which would include Paris, London, Frankfurt, New York, Miami and either Bangkok or Singapore.
He added that Lufthansa's domestic sales outfit would not escape the cost-cutting.

Among the changes, the German airline in future would concentrate its west and central German sales operation in either Frankfurt or Duesseldorf, with no final decision between the two centres yet taken, the spokesman said.

He could not confirm figures in the newspaper report suggesting that Lufthansa's domestic German market share had fallen 12 percentage points in the 1997 first quarter, adding that the figures did not come from Lufthansa.

But he noted that domestic passenger volumes had recently been lower across the German market and that Lufthansa's volumes had as a result suffered. He said this appeared to have been compensated by growth in international passenger traffic.
